turns.text: Hi, yes, my flight is delayed and this is ridiculous. I need someone to sort this out now.
I'm sorry to hear that, and I can help. First I need to verify the booking, so please give me your booking code and last name.
It's VB3N6E, Martins. Sofia Martins. Look, the Paris flight is tonight at seven fifteen and you moved it to six tomorrow morning, which is--
Thank you, Ms Martins, I have your booking. Skyline Air moved flight SK312 to tomorrow at 06:00 because of a crew shortage, and I'm sorry for the disruption.
Right, so I want a hotel voucher, three hundred dollars. The last person I spoke to already told me three hundred, so don't give me a hard time.
I can't see any promise of three hundred dollars on this booking. For an airline-caused delay that runs overnight, I can offer a hotel voucher of up to $120.
A hundred and twenty? Are you kidding me? It's a six a.m. flight, I'm not sitting in an airport all night for a hundred dollars.
I understand this is frustrating. $120 is the most I can offer for an overnight delay. If that doesn't work for you, I can arrange a supervisor callback.
Fine. Yes, call me back. But also rebook me on something else tonight, anything, a Paris flight, I don't care what time--
Rebooking on the next available flight is free, with no fare difference. I can't confirm a seat on another Paris flight from here, so the supervisor callback can look at that too.
Ugh. Okay. Just send the callback. Whatever.
To summarize, flight SK312 is delayed to tomorrow at 06:00, I've offered a hotel voucher of up to $120, and a supervisor will call you back about rebooking. Is there anything else?
